title: Cockpit Operating Space Horizon
objective: Make the already-earned causal handles ergonomic enough for Reed to steer real DME development through the Cockpit without making the Cockpit a direct controller or source of truth.
claim_ceiling: This horizon may only advance read-oriented and typed-control Cockpit ergonomics over already-earned selection, assignment, bell, authority, incident, and runtime relations. It does not establish scheduler authority, direct controller mutation, or new consequence authority.
pressure_points: Pressure typed Cockpit actions so each action previews the exact durable object and declared non-effects before creation.
Pressure assignment and horizon presentation so screen position and list order cannot silently become queue or priority semantics.
Pressure incident and stop controls so visibility remains separate from adjudication and the emergency stop remains externally controlled.
completion_criteria: Reed can inspect current horizons, selected work, assignments, bells, runtime state, authority posture, receipts, and incidents from one operating surface without the projection becoming source truth.
At least one real DME development campaign can be steered through typed selection, assignment, and manual-bell controls with exact previewed effects.
No Cockpit interaction silently creates priority, scheduler authority, direct controller mutation, or standing.
stop_conditions: A proposed Cockpit action bypasses the existing durable object boundary.
The UI requires direct mutation of controller internals to function.
Display order or convenience behavior silently becomes priority or queue semantics.
